problem_statement: Quadratic attention complexity in prefilling and excessive KV cache memory in decoding hinder efficient long-context LLM serving.
core_contributions: Introduces LServe, a unified hybrid sparse attention system for efficient long-sequence LLM serving across both prefilling and decoding stages
Proposes block-wise static + dynamic sparsity integration, converting half the attention heads into near-free 'streaming heads'
Designs a query-centric hierarchical KV page selection policy requiring only a constant number of KV pages regardless of context length
limitations_or_scope: Evaluated on A100 and L40S GPUs; focuses on decoder-only LLMs (e.g., Llama-3-8B); assumes structured sparsity compatibility with existing serving runtimes.

evidence_spans.claim_value: LServe accelerates prefilling by up to 2.9× and decoding by 1.3–2.1× over vLLM
evidence_spans.evidence_text: On average, LServe accelerates LLM prefilling by up to 2.9×\times and decoding by 1.3-2.1×\times over vLLM, maintaining long-context accuracy.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Unifies hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns for both prefilling and decoding
evidence_spans.evidence_text: This method unifies different hardware-friendly, structured sparsity patterns for both prefilling and decoding attention into a single framework

evidence_spans.claim_value: Only a constant number of KV pages is required to preserve long-context capabilities
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Additionally, we find that only a constant number of KV pages is required to preserve long-context capabilities, irrespective of context length.

problem_statement: Text embeddings enable powerful NLP applications, but similarity scores lack transparency—users cannot explain *why* two texts are deemed similar (e.g., due to semantics, paraphrase, token overlap, or bias), hindering trust and debugging in high-stakes settings.
core_contributions: Systematic taxonomy of interpretability methods for text similarity scores: space-shaping, set-based, and attribution-based approaches
Critical comparative analysis of trade-offs across methods—e.g., fidelity vs. generalizability, custom training vs. post-hoc applicability, theoretical guarantees vs. empirical faithfulness
Argument for pluralistic interpretation: treating distinct explainability methods as complementary evidence rather than competing explanations
limitations_or_scope: Focuses exclusively on interpretability of *text similarity scores*, not general model interpretability; does not propose a new method or benchmark, but surveys and analyzes existing ones.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Systematic taxonomy of interpretability methods for text similarity scores
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We give a structured overview of interpretability methods specializing in explaining those similarity scores

evidence_spans.claim_value: Critical comparative analysis of trade-offs across methods
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Methods differ in their conceptualization of interpretability, computational cost, fidelity to input tokens... space-shaping and set-based approaches result in inherently interpretable models... attribution-based methods... generalize to arbitrary models...
Rather than competing for the best explanation... we suggest to take individual methods as independent pieces of evidence for a given phenomenon
